method_observation.observation: Pilotage, tug and casualty-response probing is highest-yield when it traces how a small local service constraint or one disabled vessel propagates into channel closure, queues, cargo delay and insurance/authority decisions. Future port-service probes should measure causal leverage, not actor size or fame.

proposed_validation_probe.reason: P007 closes pilotage/towage/casualty response with high novelty. A remaining orthogonal operational gap is the administrative port-call chain coordinated by ship/port agents: notices, berth/service coordination, customs/immigration/health/port formalities, crew/spares/cash/husbandry support and disbursement accounts. This can explain non-physical delay and local information asymmetry without becoming a port-agent directory.

stop_reason: The preset questions were answered with a coherent ordinary-maneuvering and casualty-response topology. Marginal recall then shifted toward port-by-port pilot/tug rules, exact salvage clauses and awards, specific casualty law and contractor rankings; those require Evidence or would become directory/case catalog work.
